A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-model study. Their main text, figures, equations, and complete experimental and theoretical appendices can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10, CelebA, and mixed cumulant model experiments, including learning curves and architecture and optimizer comparisons in Figures 1, 3, A.3, and A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds dimension-dependent spike-recovery results in Figure 8.

M1.justification: The denoiser, loss, projected and unconstrained SGD procedures, and experimental architectures are retained. Restoring the x factor in v2 Equation (9) agrees with the derivation already present in v1 Appendix B.4; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The datasets and synthetic model family are retained. Figure 8b explicitly evaluates correlated MCM latents, but v1 Figure 1c and Appendix A.3 leave their joint latent distribution unspecified. Whether this expands data-scenario coverage or evaluates an existing scenario more explicitly is therefore uncertain.

E2.justification: The existing activation, architecture, and optimizer comparisons retain their participants. Figure 8 uses the previously evaluated SGD-trained ReLU autoencoder without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Figure 8 adds dimension sweeps: d = 50, 100, 200 for a single cumulant spike and d = 100, 200, 250 for correlated latents, with training steps normalized by d^3 and d, respectively. Existing experimental protocols in Appendix A are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 examines whether recovery trajectories across dimensions support cubic versus linear learning-time scaling. The earlier width, depth, activation, and optimizer analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing initialization counts and standard-deviation reporting are retained. Figure 8 also averages five random initializations, extending the existing MCM reporting practice without introducing a new uncertainty estimator or increasing runs for retained results.

E6.justification: Figure 8 adds six dimension-specific overlap trajectories approaching unit recovery in the single-spike and correlated-latent settings. The previously reported plots and generated samples are unchanged; the addition supplies results supporting existing scaling claims.

T1.justification: v2 restores the missing x factor in the printed spherical-gradient formula and removes Assumption 4.5's assertion that the stated derivative bounds make F globally Lipschitz. The principal propositions, sample-complexity thresholds, and appendix proof structure are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same simplicity-bias, diffusion-information-exponent, sample-complexity, correlated-latent speedup, and spherical-constraint claims. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains that Adam-trained richer networks and the single-neuron online-SGD theory should agree qualitatively rather than match exact timescales. Section 3.2 also adds a Fourier/Gabor interpretation connecting the synthetic directions to natural-image statistics.

D1.justification: Figure 8 supplies limited setup information for the new results: SGD, an overparameterized two-layer ReLU autoencoder, and the plotted dimensions. Its exact width, learning rate, and latent-correlation construction are not specified. Existing Appendix A details and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hyvärinen et al. (2009) for the natural-image interpretation and refines its characterization of Li et al. (2024) as studying Gaussian/linear denoiser bias during generalization. Other references largely undergo formatting or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain intact. Changes include local copyediting, corrected figure references, brief explanatory additions, a new asymptotic-notation subsection B.1, updated front matter, and a generic impact statement.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a conference layout with two-column main text and references, redesigned front matter and headings, and resized or repositioned figures. Figure 8 is added; Figures A.1–A.4 become Figures 4–7 with their visual content retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 8 adds empirical support for the existing scaling predictions, while the gradient correction and explicit theory–experiment qualification improve precision. These are limited gains: the central results remain unchanged, and incomplete setup documentation limits the strength and reproducibility of the new scaling evidence.
